lines.text: Power BI lets you connect tables quickly, but a model can look tidy while answering the wrong business question. Modeling starts before
you draw relationship lines: decide what process, row grain and questions the model must support.
Write a semantic-model contract: business process, intended facts, dimensions, fact grain, required questions, measure candidates,
Course 1 Power BI basics and C2-00 grain/metric-contract thinking. No advanced DAX is required.
5. New words before we use them
Semantic model: The organized layer of tables, relationships, metadata and calculations that gives business meaning to source data. Fact grain: What one
row in a fact table represents. Model contract: A short specification of what the model must represent, support and validate.

Architect's floor plan: business process sets purpose, fact grain fixes the unit of work, dimensions label the rooms, relationships connect them,
and controls inspect the finished model. A neat diagram cannot rescue a wrong grain.

Business process: online sales and returns. Decision: compare revenue, margin and return rate by product, customer, region and date.
Declare FactSales grain = one row per order line. FactReturns grain = one row per return event; do not pretend both facts have the same grain.
List dimensions needed for filtering/grouping: Product, Customer, Date and possibly Region if it is governed independently.
State the first validation controls: FactSales row count, distinct order-line key, gross/net sales totals, unmatched ProductID/CustomerID and
Only after this contract should you decide which relationships belong in Power BI.

The model is now driven by business process and grain rather than by whatever relationships Power BI auto-detects. Professional upgrade: Professional
modeling creates a reusable analytical contract. It anticipates report authors, refresh behavior, security, future measures and validation-not only today's visual.
1. Starting with charts. | 2. Creating relationships because matching column names exist. | 3. Mixing multiple grains in one fact without deciding
what one row means. | 4. Treating a PBIX opening without errors as validation.

5. New words before we use them
Fact table: A table representing measurable business events or states, usually on the many side of relationships. Dimension table: A table describing
business entities used to filter/group facts, usually on the one side. Surrogate key: A technical key created to identify dimension rows when business keys
are unsuitable or need historical versions.

dimension. | 4. Creating a one-to-many relationship before checking the 'one' key.

PBM-A3 - Star schema in professional BI
Database source schemas are often normalized for transactions, not analytics. A clean star reduces ambiguous paths and makes
filters/measures easier for report authors to understand.
Arrange conformed dimensions around facts, avoid fact-to-fact shortcuts, handle multiple facts deliberately, and recognize when a snowflake or
5. New words before we use them
Star schema: A model with fact tables surrounded by dimensions connected through clear one-to-many relationships. Conformed dimension: A dimension
whose meaning/key can consistently filter multiple fact tables. Snowflake: A dimension split into related normalized tables rather than flattened into one
Star diagram + fact-grain notes + filter-path review + explain-back. VIDEO SUPPORT: 02:18-15:35

Railway hub: facts are the central stations and conformed dimensions are direct spokes. Filters should have one understandable route to each
fact; avoid detours that create competing paths or mixed-grain shortcuts.

Put DimDate, DimProduct and DimCustomer around FactSales.
FactReturns stays a separate fact at return-event grain. Relate it through compatible dimensions or a deliberate business key strategy; do not
MonthlyTargets stays a higher-grain fact connected only to dimensions whose grain it supports, such as Month/Region.
Use conformed dimensions so Sales and Returns interpret Product/Customer/Date consistently.
Sketch filter paths before building. Every important visual should have one understandable route from dimension to fact.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A star-schema sketch showing facts at their own grains and shared dimensions without ambiguous fact-to-fact shortcuts.
Dimensions become the reusable filter surface; facts remain separate measurable processes. Professional upgrade: Good star schemas balance usability,
performance and source constraints. Deviations are allowed when justified, but the default should be easy to reason about.
1. One giant flat table by default. | 2. Fact-to-fact many-to-many because both tables contain OrderID. | 3. Connecting targets to transaction rows
without grain control. | 4. Snowflaking tiny descriptive hierarchies without benefit.

5. New words before we use them
Filter propagation: How a filter on one model table affects rows in related tables. Cross-filter direction: The direction in which a relationship allows filters to
travel. Active relationship: The default relationship path used for filter propagation.

Many-to-many can be legitimate, but it is also a common symptom of dirty keys or mixed grain. Changing cardinality to make an error
disappear can create ambiguous or inflated analysis.

5. New words before we use them
Many-to-many relationship: A relationship where matching values can repeat on both sides. Bridge table: A table used to resolve a genuine many-to-many
relationship by storing valid key combinations. Higher-grain fact: A fact table summarized at a broader level than another fact, such as Region-Month targets.
Diagnosis note + bridge/higher-grain sketch + key checks + filter test + explain-back. VIDEO: intentionally book-led for this lesson

Door-count rule: the one side must contain one trustworthy key per entity; the many side may repeat. If both sides repeat, diagnose why before
choosing a bridge or higher-grain pattern - never use M:M as a cleanup shortcut.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
DimSalesperson is one row per SalespersonID. DimRegion is one row per RegionID.
One salesperson can belong to several regions and one region can have several salespeople. This is a genuine many-to-many dimension
Create BridgeSalespersonRegion with one row per valid salesperson-region assignment. Connect each dimension 1:* to the bridge.
Do not use this pattern to excuse duplicate ProductID rows in DimProduct. Duplicate product keys are a different problem.
Validate bridge uniqueness at the pair grain and test a simple salesperson/region selection for expected membership.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A model decision that explains whether the repeated key is a defect, higher-grain fact or genuine many-to-many relationship.

5. New words before we use them
Role-playing dimension: One business entity used in multiple roles relative to a fact. Inactive relationship: A model relationship that does not propagate filters
by default. USERELATIONSHIP: A DAX function that activates an existing relationship for a calculation.

5. New words before we use them
Date dimension: A table containing one row per calendar date plus attributes used for filtering/grouping. Continuous date range: Every date between model
start and end exists with no gaps. Auto date/time: Power BI behavior that can create hidden date tables/hierarchies for date columns.

roles. Missing or duplicate dates bend every time-based comparison built on top.

PBM-A8 - Power Query architecture for BI models
A semantic model can be clean while its Power Query layer is fragile. Mixing source connection, cleaning, business logic and final load into
one opaque query makes refresh/debugging harder.
Separate source/staging/model-ready queries; set types deliberately; reuse references; document transformations; understand when query
folding can push work to a capable source.
C2-01 Power Query concepts if you took C2A sequentially. This lesson restates the BI-model-specific architecture from first principles.
5. New words before we use them
Staging query: A query used to establish source scope/types/basic cleaning before downstream model-ready queries. Query folding: Power Query translating
supported transformations into operations executed by the source system. Reference query: A new query based on another query's result/steps, useful for
Query dependency sketch + Applied Steps evidence + folding note + row/key controls + explain-back. VIDEO SUPPORT: 04:54-13:36; 17:50-28:25; 33:35-35:17

Course 2A | C2_03 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 1
C2_03 Module Test - Protected Review RC4
Open only after a saved genuine attempt. Diagnose the weak competency, then close this review and perform a
changed retry.
PBM-A1
Business process/decision, every fact grain, intended dimensions/filter questions, relationship/date-role assumptions, and
independent validation controls. The contract should let a reviewer predict the model before seeing the PBIX.
PBM-A2
The one side of a one-to-many relationship must identify an entity uniquely. Duplicate keys create ambiguous attribute/filter
meaning and can force invalid cardinality or duplicate propagation. Investigate cause before choosing a documented repair.
PBM-A3
A star gives filters a clear dimension-to-fact route at declared grains. Fact-to-fact links often mix grains, create ambiguous
filter paths, and make additive measures easy to double count.
PBM-A4
Check both fact grains, relationship existence/active state/cardinality/direction, key coverage/orphans, and a tiny known filter
case. Do not enable Both merely because one visual did not respond.
PBM-A5
Legitimate when the business relationship itself is many-to-many or when a bridge/higher-grain pattern is required. It is not
legitimate as a shortcut around a duplicate key that should have been unique.
PBM-A6
The report question and expected default slicer behavior choose the role. If most measures mean Order Date, make that
default/active; expose Ship Date through a deliberate alternate relationship/role or duplicated role-playing dimension as
designed.
PBM-A7
Unique date key, continuous range covering facts, correct data type/attributes, and tested relationships to each fact role. Also
reconcile boundary dates and avoid hidden auto-date behavior becoming the undocumented authority.
PBM-A8
Staging establishes source scope/types/basic cleaning while keeping lineage; downstream/model-ready queries apply
reusable business transforms and load only what the model needs. Record row/key controls across the dependency chain.
PBM-A9
At minimum: source/fact row counts, one-side uniqueness, unmatched keys, relationship/filter propagation tests, date-role
tests, material measure/total reconciliation, and documented exceptions/release decision.
PBM-A10
Otherwise an optimization can silently change the business result. Capture a correct baseline, inspect
model/cardinality/relationship/analyzer evidence, change one thing, rerun the same controls, and retain it only with result
parity.

2. Expected reasoning path
Begin with three grains: FactSales = one order line; FactReturns = one return event; FactMonthlyTargets = one
Region-Month target. A direct fact-to-fact shortcut is not a star-schema substitute.
P04 is an exact duplicate in the supplied dirty product file. That makes a documented deterministic dedupe possible for this
fixture, but the model must first prove why the duplicate is safe; M:M is not the repair.
P99 contributes 3,248.52 of gross sales. Dropping unmatched products can leave a professional-looking model while
changing the controlled total. Preserve an unknown/exception path until ownership resolves the key.
OrderDate and ShipDate produce different monthly row/totals. The active/default date role must follow the report question;
prove the alternate role with a tiny known filter case.
Region-Month targets are a higher-grain fact. Create/use a conformed Region and Date/Month path so a target is not
multiplied by transaction lines. Reconcile target rows before any target-vs-actual measure.
3. Critical failures
• Uses M:M or Both to bypass duplicate P04.
• Drops P99 with an INNER JOIN or filter and still signs off gross sales.
• Joins Region-Month target rows to sales transaction rows and sums repeated target.
• Treats Returns as if it shared Sales line grain without an explicit key/date contract.
• Chooses OrderDate/ShipDate because a visual “looks right” without a boundary filter test.
• Releases without row/key/money reconciliation and exception evidence.

absence of duplicate billing does not make Billing a dimension.

pack checks all source rows, orphan counts and charge controls as well as decision KPIs.
VisitDate and DischargeDate answer different questions. The period counts differ at boundaries, so the default role must be
explicit and the alternate path tested.
Specialty-Month targets require a conformed Specialty/Date route. Encounter ChargeBase and Billing BillAmount are
different measures/populations; a mismatch between 122,665 and 88,257.60 is not itself an error.
